headline: Nasdaq-100: an unresolved hawkish repricing meets a closed market, leaving tail risk at the low-band floor into the reopen
body:
This assessment falls inside the weekend CME halt, so no live NQ price path exists and no mean-reversion failure can be developing. The anchor is Friday's completed session, re-verified this hour from the index history rather than the quote page, which was serving a stale cached session: NDX opened 29,545.90, reached 29,752.78, fell to 29,383.92 and closed 29,433.43, down 0.70% from a 29,641.56 previous close. The close sits about 50 points off the low of a 369-point range. Verified session reporting describes the path as an early advance of as much as 0.5% that reversed, with selling accelerating through the afternoon after the Jackson Hole keynote. The Nasdaq Composite finished -0.52%, the S&P 500 -0.25% and the Dow -0.02%, and all three still closed the week higher. VIX closed 14.43 within a 14.13-14.84 range, carrying no volatility premium into the weekend.

The macro driver is a hawkish repricing rather than a price-path event. The Federal Reserve's published keynote by Chairman Kevin Warsh states that "inflation is running above our 2 percent target" and that policymakers "must be confident that underlying inflation is moving to our objective, clearly and at sufficient speed. Otherwise, we have work to do." The market response was concentrated at the front end: the 2-year yield rose about 8 basis points, the 10-year 4 basis points to 4.72% and the 30-year 2 basis points to 5.21%, while implied odds of a September rate increase moved from about 35% to about 57%. The H.15 release shows official constant-maturity yields through 27 August at 4.20% for the 2-year, 4.38% for the 5-year, 4.67% for the 10-year and 5.19% for the 30-year, so the repricing is a Friday market move that the official series has not yet absorbed. Verified weekend reporting adds an important qualifier: bond investors at several large managers are described as sceptical of the hike wagers, and prediction-market odds sit near a coin flip. That is an unresolved two-way debate, not a settled directional catalyst.

Cross-asset evidence conflicts rather than aligns. The latest session left the semiconductor complex uniformly lower, none of the seven tracked names positive, with NVDA down 4.57%, ARM down 6.33% and INTC down 2.85%, while the megacap tape was split five to three higher, led by AMZN up 3.97%. Technology fell 1.41% while Communication Services and Consumer Cyclical both rose more than 1.3%. Under the risk definitions in force, conflicting internals reduce directional conviction and raise Stress; they are not an amplifier of the pathological price path Tail measures. WTI near 83.44 dollars ended last week about 4% lower, with verified reporting describing the Iran situation as a sanctions and economic confrontation rather than an imminent threat to physical supply, and improved Strait of Hormuz flows. No fresh geopolitical discontinuity is verified as of this cutoff.

None of the amplifiers that would justify a higher Tail are present: there is no observed persistent directional efficiency, no shallow-pullback sequence, no repeated extension after failed retracements, and no open market in which any of those could be forming. Tail therefore rests at the low-band floor of 5 and the mapped policy state is EA_ON. Stress at 31 reflects the untested front-end repricing meeting a data-heavy week: ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS on Tuesday, ADP and the Broadcom report on Wednesday, ISM Services on Thursday and August payrolls on Friday. One narrow observation window is flagged across the 22:00-23:30 UTC Sunday reopen, where that repricing first meets thin liquidity and two-way gap risk. Monday 31 August is also month-end, and the UK summer bank holiday leaves London closed, thinning European depth through the day. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment, covering the weekend halt from Saturday evening through the hour before this one. The series was uniformly green with Tail fixed at 5, dominant mode normal, and Stress confined to a 25-30 band that drifted up only in the final hours. Confidence decayed from 65 to 58 through the overnight hours as published evidence aged across the closed market, then recovered through 64, 72 and 80 to 86 as primary sources were re-verified on each hourly refresh. No hour in the window contained an observable NQ price path.
outlookSummary: The next three projected hours remain inside the weekend CME halt, where no price path can form; Tail stays at the low-band floor of 5 while Stress holds at 31 and Confidence eases from 86 to 84. From the projected 22:00 UTC reopen the conditional Tail lifts to 12, still inside the low band and far below the block threshold, covering the first live test of Friday's front-end repricing. It then eases through 11 and 10 across the Asian session to an overnight low of 8, lifts through 9 and 10 into a continental-only European morning thinned by the UK bank holiday, and reaches a projected peak of 15 across the 13:30 UTC U.S. cash open, where opening-auction imbalance meets month-end rebalancing on the final session of August. The window closes at 14 as month-end market-on-close flow builds into the U.S. afternoon. Every projected hour maps to EA_ON and green; Stress peaks at 36 in the moderate band and Confidence decays to 70 at the far end of the projection.
